subject: Insurance
title: The Lloyd's Bell
description: A 60-second lesson on The Lloyd's Bell.

hook.text: The Lutine Bell at Lloyd's of London is rung once for bad news, twice for good. It was rung once on September 11, 2001.

buildup.text: The bell was salvaged from HMS Lutine, which sank in 1799 carrying gold insured by Lloyd's. It became their symbol.

discovery.text: The single toll for bad news alerted the trading floor to major losses. Two tolls meant a missing ship had been found.

twist.text: The bell is rarely rung now—electronic communication replaced it. But on catastrophic days, tradition returns.

climax.text: The Lutine Bell represents insurance's core promise: when disaster strikes, someone is ready to pay.

punchline.text: One toll for disaster. The Lutine Bell marks every major loss.

quiz.question: What does one ring of the Lutine Bell mean?
